requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST use
the current workspace source at book-render time and explicitly identify its
contents as current workspace source notes.
rationale:
The subject has two obligations. The notes view must use the current workspace source at book-render time. It must also explicitly identify its contents as current workspace source notes.

`src/execution_coverage/notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[each_render_reads_current_notes_and_keeps_recorded_reviews_without_writing]` is marked `{test}` for the subject and covers both.

- **Current source at render time.** The test writes `code.rs` with the original explanation and saves recorded reviews. It renders once, then edits `code.rs` on disk to say "Updated platform". It renders a second time through the `render` helper, which calls `pages` on the real fixture directory. It asserts that the second render contains "Updated platform explanation.". It also asserts that the part of the content before "Review:" no longer contains "Original platform explanation.". A render that cached, or used the first render's source, would fail these assertions. The recorded-review checks guard against stale notes being passed off as current.
- **Explicit identification.** The test asserts that the content contains "Current workspace source notes". The `pages` code emits the header "**Current workspace source notes**, read at book-render time", so the label is asserted on the rendered chapter. The capitalised form of the phrase is an acceptable reading of the requirement's wording.

I found no other distinct input classes or failure cases in the requirement text. The parent requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` (the per-file path identification) is cited as context only, so it needs no check here.
